messages:
incident-bot: 🔴 ALERT: Dedicated pool 'eu-west-1-prod-ded-3' p99 latency breach detected. p99=3.2s (SLO=1.2s). Queue depth rising. Paging oncall: @olivia_oncall

olivia_oncall: I'm on it. seeing streaming stalls in the dashboard. Any immediate customer impact? Lina, can you correlate with open CS tickets?

lina_support: quick check — two customers reported degraded streaming responses starting ~08:02 UTC (partial frames, stalls). No full errors yet, but user-perceived latency for long responses spiked.

sam_eng-sre: looking at infra metrics now. Pool CPU/GPU saturation ~98%. autoscaler attempted scale at 08:03 but handshake/warmup timeout occurred. warmup latency ~14-22s for new workers. p95 is 1.05s but p99 blown out to 3.2s.

jia_runtime: logs from runtime show lots of requests hitting hot prefix cache misses. KV cache miss rate jumped from 8% -> 63% during burst. Continuous batching backlog increased. Key lines: ```[08:03:12] pool=ded-3 HANDSHAKE_START id=0x9f...
[08:03:26] pool=ded-3 WARMUP_DONE id=0x9f... warmup_time=22.4s```

amar_platform: autoscaler events: tried to add 6 nodes at 08:03:05, cloud provider provisioned VMs but agent registration slowed; handshake retries hit our 20s threshold, autoscaler aborted new nodes and queued a retry. Looks like provisioning jitter in region.

olivia_oncall: immediate mitigation options? can we fallback traffic to a compatible lower-capacity model variant or route to another region?

sam_eng-sre: two quick mitigations: 1) throttle backend burst rate for non-critical customers (reduce concurrency tokens), 2) reroute a % of traffic to eu-west-1-fallback pool with older quantized model (slightly lower quality). I can TTL an override. Thoughts?

jia_runtime: reroute is lowest-risk. Fallback variant supports streaming. But we need a graceful mapper so tokens and billing remain consistent. Also can we enable aggressive KV prefill for hot prefixes — we have prewarm script we can run against expected prefixes.

amar_platform: I can force-register the partially provisioned nodes (manual handshake accept) to get capacity online faster. That bypasses autoscaler abort logic. It'll be a bit risky (nodes may be unhealthy) but better than SLO breach for customers. Need eng-sre + runtime signoff.

olivia_oncall: @sam_eng-sre proceed with reroute + throttle. @amar_platform prepare forced registration but hold action until we confirm reroute. Lina, message affected customers with an update.

lina_support: drafting message now. ETA 3m.

sam_eng-sre: applied routing override: ```/routing/production -> weight: ded-3 60%, fallback-pool 40%``` and set per-customer concurrency caps for tier=free to 1. Command: `redwoodctl route update --override burst-mitigation`

incident-bot: Notice: routing override applied by sam_eng-sre at 08:07:21

jia_runtime: after routing change, KV miss rate on ded-3 dropped to 35%, queue depth started falling from 420 -> 120. Streaming stalls still seen for long sequences but p99 has improved to 1.9s.

sam_eng-sre: OK p99 trending down. Still seeing intermittent 2.0-2.5s stalls tied to some large-sequence requests (seq_len > 2k). Might need to cap streaming chunking size or lower max tokens for the shortest term.

amar_platform: I'm ready to force-register 4 nodes. If we do that, we should run quick healthchecks: `curl /health` + sample inference smoke test. I recommend bringing nodes into a warm state with prewarm runner (script below):
```bash
for prefix in $(cat hot_prefixes.txt); do 
  redwood-prewarm --pool ded-3 --prefix "$prefix" --concurrency 4 &
done
```

olivia_oncall: go ahead with force-register + prewarm once sam confirms it's safe. Sam?

sam_eng-sre: confirm. Amar, register nodes and run the `smoke-infer` test (3 short prompts + 1 long). If smoke passes, proceed with prewarm. I'll monitor p95/p99 and cutover weight back to 80/20 when stable.

amar_platform: executing manual registration... `node-342 registered` `node-343 registered` -> running smoke tests...
devops-bot: smoke tests: node-342 PASSED, node-343 PASSED (latency within expected).

jia_runtime: starting prewarm against top 50 prefixes now. Prewarm logs show progressive KV fill and kernel cache hits increasing. Warmup time per node reduced to ~4s for small prefixes.

sam_eng-sre: adjusting routing weights to 80% ded-3 / 20% fallback at 08:16:40. p99 now at 1.4s, p95 at 0.95s. Queue depth ~30. Streaming frames stable with minor jitter.

olivia_oncall: great. I'll annotate the pager: initial breach window 08:02-08:17 UTC. Impact: degraded streaming for a subset of long responses for ~10-15% of requests in ded-3. No customer data loss.

lina_support: sent customer comms: "We've mitigated a latency issue affecting streaming responses in eu-west-1; we routed traffic to fallback capacity and scaled capacity. We're monitoring and will follow up with postmortem."

sam_eng-sre: immediate root causes: burst of large-seq requests + autoscaler abort due to provider registration jitter + high KV cache miss amplification. Short-term mitigations taken: routing override, throttle non-critical customers, forced node registration, prewarm run.

olivia_oncall: owners for follow-up: sam_eng-sre (incident lead), amar_platform (autoscaler tuning), jia_runtime (cache/prefill improvements), lina_support (customer comms). We'll file postmortem and action items.

bob_product: flagging product impact: consider soft-limits on sequence length for free/low-tier customers to avoid noisy neighbor issues.

amar_platform: action item: increase autoscaler handshake timeout and add provider retry jitter mitigation. Ticket: PLAT-4321.

jia_runtime: action item: implement proactive hot-prefix prewarm when autoscaler triggers scale up; add telemetry to correlate prefix miss rates with bursts. Ticket: RUNTIME-1189.

sam_eng-sre: I'll draft a short-runbook for oncall: when p99 breach + queue depth >200 + autoscaler aborted => apply route override to fallback, throttle non-critical, force-register nodes, prewarm hot prefixes.

olivia_oncall: thanks team. Marking this thread as oncall-handoff to sam_eng-sre for postmortem. I'll stay available if escalation needed.

incident-bot: Incident acknowledged and assigned: lead=sam_eng-sre, severity=sev2, start_ts=2246789012, status=mitigated

sam_eng-sre: closing live mitigation. Will open postmortem doc and link it here when ready.
